r: Letting friction between your two strongest engineers run another quarter of quiet standoffs will cost the whole team. Google's Project Aristotle studied 180 teams and found psychological safety mattered more than who was on them. Don't try to referee personalities; referee interfaces. Most senior-engineer feuds are design-authority disputes disguised as grudges, so a clear ownership boundary document naming who decides what usually drains much of the heat. Meet each engineer separately first. You will likely find each believes the other is slowing delivery. Then schedule a joint session with a written agenda and one shared, measurable deliverable. Tuckman's 1965 model calls this storming; teams that skip it rarely reach performing. Watch code review comment threads, because tone shows there before people resign. If one threatens to leave, replacing a senior engineer often costs six to nine months of salary. Mediate early, not after someone has gone.
